summary: This script checks whether question sidecars (`.questions.json` files) are still valid after their source articles have been edited. It detects three problems: stale sidecars where the source has changed since they were generated, orphaned sidecars whose source file no longer exists, and coverage gaps where published articles have no sidecars yet. It reports these issues and optionally exits with failure if the `--strict` flag is set and stale or orphaned files are found.

explanations.36: Since this is an ES module, `import.meta.url` gives the current file's URL; `fileURLToPath` converts it to a filesystem path so we can find the directory it lives in.
explanations.39: This checks if `--strict` appears in the command-line arguments; `process.argv` is an array of everything passed to the script.
explanations.44: These arguments tell git to list files it knows about (cached and untracked), excluding things like `.gitignore` files, and to output results separated by null bytes instead of newlines (null bytes handle filenames with spaces safely).
explanations.56: This runs the git command and splits the result on null bytes, then filters out empty strings left over from the trailing null byte.
explanations.64: This filters out any path that contains `/files/` as a directory segment, because files in a `files` folder are documentation examples, not the actual sidecars that sit next to `index.md`.
explanations.81: This strips off the `.questions.json` extension to get the source file path — if the sidecar is `blog/post.questions.json`, the source is `blog/post`.
explanations.109: This hashes the current contents of the source file and compares it to the hash stored in the sidecar; if they don't match, the sidecar is stale because the source changed.
explanations.113: This regex checks if the source path is inside an i18n folder (like `i18n/es/...`); if it is, the first capture group extracts the locale code.
explanations.125: This finds all published blog posts (draft posts are already filtered out by `loadPosts()`) and checks which ones don't have a `.questions.json` file yet.
explanations.138: For each locale folder that exists, this finds all translated articles that are eligible for questions but don't have a localized sidecar yet.
explanations.146: This boolean is true if there's anything important to report — stale sidecars, orphaned sidecars, or coverage gaps — so we only print the summary if something is actionable or quiet mode is off.
explanations.154: This builds a space-separated string of quoted file paths so they can be used directly in the shell command printed next.
explanations.167: This loop counts how many missing sidecars belong to each locale so we can print a per-locale summary instead of one giant list.
explanations.185: Since showing all missing sidecars could produce hundreds of lines, this caps the list at 10 items to keep the output readable during commits.
